main_text.p: tur; quàm grave & immedicabile [illegible, ~8 letters] scandalum: tota res ista vergit in obstinatam quandam invidam & odium fidei, & certam perniciem hominum: Christus, quod non debet, tributum solvit, ne scandalizet: [illegible, ~10 letters] nos nullo modo debitas terras si spoliemus, vexemus, prædemur, nullum ne justum timebimus scandalū? res ipsa satis clamat per se; omnino verum est, quod Gregorius scribit: [illegible, ~9 letters] qui fidem asperitatibus propagari volunt, suas non Dei causas probantur attendere. Justus Lipsius lib.2.de constant.cap.22.de inaudita Romana feritate hæc habet, Pauculi Iberi ante annos 8o in vastas illas & novas terras delati, quæ funera (Deus bone) ediderunt: quas strages: nec de causis aut de jure belli disfero, tantùm de eventis. cerno ingens illud terrarum spatium (quod vidisse magnū sit, non dicam vicisse) à vicenis tricenisque militibus pervadi, & passim inermes illos greges sterni, ut segetem à falce. Ubi tu es insularum maxima Cuba? tu Haijtę? [?] tu Jucajæ?
{ } Left-margin notes on this page are cropped; fragments visible only.

page.notes: Page number "45" read as printed, the top figures are slightly unclear. Left margin notes are cut off by the page edge; only fragments are visible and they are shown as illegible, with approximate letter counts. Italic passage in the text is the citation "Justus Lipsius lib.2.de constant.cap.22.de inaudita". "Haijtę" is uncertain; the reading of the final letter is doubtful. The line "quæ" at the bottom is recorded as the catchword and not repeated in the text. The text is one continuous paragraph from the previous page with no printed indents on this page.
